question.leadin: This dynasty converted the Schonbrunn (shurn-brun) Palace from a hunting lodge to the permanent imperial summer residence where Franz Joseph died.
question.text: Name this dynasty that inbred so much they developed a namesake chin. Under this dynasty's Charles V, their empire stretched from Spain to Hungary.
question.clue: The founder of this house gained significant parcels of land after his victory at the Battle of Marchfeld, and the death of a later member of this house served as the extinction of its non-Styrian branch.

swap.text: The Spaniards were led by Philip II and other kings of this dynasty. This royal house also had an Austrian branch and sported a namesake "jaw" due to incest.
swap.clue: In the 19th century, this family took the title "King of Lombardy-Venetia".

question.text: "Great Germans" and "Small Germany" advocates debated during the Frankfurt Assembly about uniting Germany with Austria. That happened in this 1938 Hitler-sponsored event after the Sudetenland annexation.
question.clue: Kurt von Schuschnigg was replaced by Arthur Seyss-Inquart the day before this event, which gathered 99.7% approval in a plebiscite a month after it happened.

swap.leadin: After failing to accomplish this event with a bomb, Nedeljko Cabrinovic [neh-dyell-koh kah-bree- noh-vich] failed to commit suicide by swallowing weak cyanide and jumping into a five-inch deep river.
swap.text: Name this June 28, 1914 event that was accomplished by Gavrilo Princip. It triggered anti-Serbian demonstrations in Austria-Hungary, the July Crisis, and, eventually, World War I.
swap.answerHtml: assassination (or murder or equivalents) of Franz Ferdinand (prompt on partial answer)
swap.clue: Thomas McMahon was convicted for his role in this event, which had been attempted a year prior via sniper and was carried out via a radio-controlled bomb in Donegal Bay.

question.text: This first Austro-Hungarian Kaiser und Koenig ruled for 68 years. The assassination of his heir Archduke Ferdinand led to his invasion of Serbia and the start of World War I.
question.clue: This man's reign saw the provinces of Venetia and Lombardy ceded to Italy.

swap.leadin: One leader from this empire increased censorship by issuing the Carlsbad Decree.
swap.text: Name this empire home to a statesman who hosted the post-Napoleonic Congress of Vienna, Klemens von Metternich. This empire's combination with Hungary was dissolved after World War I.
swap.clue: This state deliberately provoked an 1846 serf rebellion in order to counter revolutionary szlachta.

question.text: Name this Austrian queen whose inheritance was justified by her father Charles VI's Pragmatic Sanction. Her accession was disputed in the War of Austrian Succession.
question.clue: Wenzel Kaunitz accepted Zator and Auschwitz in the first partition of Poland as the advisor of this ruler.

swap.leadin: This empire used "K.U.K." as its official abbreviation on ships and various articles of state in order to reflect political realities of split power.
swap.text: Name this European empire that was formed by a namesake 1867 compromise. It was one of the members of the pre-World War I Triple Alliance along with Italy and the German Empire.
swap.clue: The phrase "k.u.k" was used as a term for this country's system of government after the Ausgleich.

question.text: In Vienna, one of the first demands of the revolution was the resignation of this man. This Austrian Chancellor used censorship and the secret police to maintain stability in the post-Napoleonic era.

swap.leadin: The Ostend Company was dissolved in return for the recognition of this document, which Charles Albert of Bavaria rejected.
swap.text: Name this 1713 edict by which Holy Roman Emperor Charles VI declared that his daughter could inherit the dominion of the Habsburgs if no son were born to him.
swap.clue: This edict issued by Charles VI permitting Maria Theresa to inherit the throne.

question.leadin: A building in this town was converted into a convent for Discalced Carmelites.
question.text: Name this town where the Crown Prince of Austria, Rudolf, killed himself with his lover Mary Vetsera in a hunting lodge.

swap.leadin: Due to being only five foot tall, this leader was derisively called "Millimetternich," a portmanteau of "millimeter" and "Klemens von Metternich."
swap.text: Name this Austrian who banned all parties except his Fatherland Front in the May Constitution. He was succeeded by Kurt von Schuschnigg after his assassination by the Nazis in the botched 1934 July Putsch.
swap.clue: This dictator absorbed the Heimwehr of Prince Starhemberg to establish the Fatherland Front, but was assassinated by Otto Planetta during the July Putsch.

question.leadin: A minister of this ruler freed peasants from their compulsory robota labor by breaking up church-owned estates in a process known as "Raabization."
question.text: Name this ruler who also introduced one of the first compulsory public school systems. This ruler was officially designated as heir in an edict issued by Charles VI.
question.answerHtml: Maria Theresa of Austria [or Maria Theresa Walburgia Amalia Christina]
question.clue: This ruler conceded lost territory in one war in the Treaty of Hubertusburg.

swap.text: This Austrian emperor created the Dual Monarchy with Hungary and reigned for over 60 years. Franz Ferdinand was the nephew and heir of this ruler until his assassination.
swap.clue: This ruler. After the death of Felix of Schwarzenberg, Alexander Bach became the leading policymaker of his reign.

question.leadin: Name these powerful women in 19th-century Europe.
question.text: This wife of Emperor Franz Joseph of Austria-Hungary coerced her husband into the compromise that formed the Dual Monarchy. This Habsburg fashion icon was assassinated by the anarchist Luigi Lucheni in 1898.

swap.text: Germany's World War I version of an entrenching tool, called a Feldspaten, was similar to the MPL-50.Feldspatens were manufactured by this Austrian weapons manufacturer known for their easy-to-use handguns.

question.leadin: Try to keep track of all those damn World War I treaties so you can answer this bonus.
question.text: Hungary, Czechoslovakia, Poland, and Yugoslavia were recognized by the newly formed Austria in this treaty, which shares its name with a 1570 treaty made during the French wars of religion.

swap.text: In the years leading up to World War I, the Austro-Hungarian military Chief of Staff was this bonehead, who got Austria to declare war on Serbia and then screwed up basically everything in the first half of the war.
swap.answerHtml: Franz Conrad von Hoetzendorf [or Franz Xaver Josef Conrad von Hoetzendorf; accept von Hoetzendorf]

question.leadin: This leader came to power after his predecessor resigned in protest of the Ninth-of-May Constitution.
question.text: Name this leader who became the first communist President of Czechoslovakia in 1948 after deposing Edvard Benes during Victorious February.

swap.text: For years, Haider was governor of this southern Austrian state, where he attracted controversy for his adversarial stance toward its native Slovene population.
